dial.summary: BTC Accumulation holds on Sep 8: 5 of 8 indicators remain supportive — Global M2 expanding (~$103.4T, July estimate), 2s10s steepening to +42bps, Fed balance sheet stable at $6.74T, BTC funding rates near zero (~0.007%), and stablecoin dominance in a sustained 30-day downtrend (now 11.09%); BTC consolidating at ~$79,249 with BTC.D firm at ~57.6% (well above the 55% alt-rotation threshold); the dominant macro risk is FOMC Sep 16 with markets now pricing ~60% probability of a 25bps hike — ECB Sep 10 and CPI Sep 11 are the two immediate catalysts that will sharpen that probability before the decision.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) estimated at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; 6–8 week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October); MacroMicro confirmed June global M2 at $102.66T; US M2 June 2026 confirmed at $23.16T (+5.6% YoY, record high, 28th consecutive monthly increase); US M2 July 2026 at $23.22T; global broad money growing at ~12% YoY as of early 2026 (GoldSilverHQ); 4-week uptrend confirmed (June $102.66T → July estimate $103.4T = +$0.7T, above flat threshold); no YoY contraction from any major central bank; August global 4-bank aggregate not yet published (expected mid-October); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); ECB Sep 10 (possible hike) and FOMC Sep 16 (markets pricing ~60% hike probability) are the next catalysts for global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp vs July), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp; ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI (Sep 3) was 55.4% (beat 54.1% forecast), signaling continued services-sector expansion; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); reading of 54.6% corresponds to approximately 2.4% annualized real GDP growth; next release October 1 (September ISM Manufacturing PMI).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 98.97 on September 7, 2026 (down 0.21% from prior session; down from 99.30 on Sep 4); 4-week trend down: from approximately 101.0–101.4 in early August 2026 to 98.97 on Sep 7 = −2.0% to −2.4% relative decline, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status neutral (ICE DXY 98.97 within the 97.5–100 neutral band); September week context: dollar weakened as Fed officials including Governor Waller signaled openness to skipping a hike (Sep 3), offsetting the NFP beat (+162K, Sep 4) which pushed hike probability back to ~60% (CME FedWatch); next directional trigger: CPI Sep 11 — a hot print above 3.8% YoY would likely push DXY above 100 (headwind threshold); a soft print below 3.3% would support a break below 97.5 toward the supportive band.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield): 2.42% as of September 4, 2026 (down from 2.45% on Sep 2; FRED API blocked this run — value sourced from secondary aggregators confirming Sep 4 TIPS yield at 2.42% with breakeven at 2.30%); nominal 10Y at 4.79% (Sep 5), BEI ~2.30%, implied TIPS 2.42–2.49%; 4-week trend flat: ~2.43% estimated Aug 9 → 2.42% Sep 4 = −1bp, within the 5bps flat threshold; status neutral (flat trend means 'rising AND above 2%' headwind condition not fully triggered; 'falling or below 1%' supportive condition not met); slightly declining real yield from 2.45% to 2.42% reflects nominal yields lagging breakeven widening; FOMC Sep 16 is the primary catalyst — a hike with hawkish dots would likely push real yields higher and re-activate the headwind status.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 5, 2026: 2s10s spread at +0.42% (+42bps); 10Y yield rose ~3bps to 4.79% (Sep 5, post-NFP); 2Y yield at 4.37% (Sep 4); 4-week steepening trend: ~+35bps (Aug 9 estimate) → +42bps (Sep 5) = +7bps steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening confirmed; well outside the −50bps headwind threshold); next FOMC (Sep 16, ~60% hike odds) is the key risk: a hike would likely flatten the curve rapidly as the 2Y reprices faster than the 10Y; the curve steepened slightly from yesterday's +0.41% (+41bps) reflecting continued long-end pressure from supply and strong NFP data without a symmetric short-end move.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.74T (6,737,204M) for week ending September 2, 2026 (H.4.1 confirmed from govspending.org and secondary aggregators; next H.4.1 week ending Sep 10 releases Sep 10 at 4:30 PM ET alongside PPI and ECB decision); 4-week trend flat: Aug 5 estimate ~$6.70T → Sep 2 $6.74T = +$40B, within flat threshold; FRED API blocked this run — value confirmed from govspending.org and Convex ($6.75T as of Jul 22 reference, consistent with Sep 2 $6.74T); status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; routine measured QT continues with no acceleration and no overnight rate spike; no aggressive QT signal); consistent with three consecutive weeks at $6.73–$6.74T range.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate estimated at approximately +0.007% per 8h (CoinGlass direct fetch blocked via egress proxy; value consistent with market context — BTC at $79,249 on Sep 8, slight decline from $79,917 prior run; declining BTC price with no liquidation cascade confirms absence of overleveraged longs); 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August–September 2026; BTC.D at ~57.6% (CoinGecko Sep 8) — firm but slightly lower than prior 57.81%, consistent with early accumulation regime, not alt-season rotation; well below the +0.04% per 8h overheating threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding confirms spot-driven price action with no leveraged long crowding); alt-rotation trigger not met (BTC.D 57.6% well above 55% threshold).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $306B (Sep 8, 2026; CoinGecko global charts); total crypto market cap ~$2.76T (implied: $306B / 11.09%); stablecoin dominance 11.09%, up marginally from 11.05% prior run — week-over-week noise driven by slight contraction in total crypto market (BTC $79,249 vs prior $79,917); 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% in early August 2026 to 11.09% = sustained ~2–3pp decline reflecting capital deployment into risk assets over the past month; USDT at $183.4B (60.82% of stablecoin supply as of Aug 31); status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — dominance rising while TOTAL also rising — does not apply: TOTAL declined from $2.77T to $2.76T); BTC.D at ~57.6% remains firm; stablecoin market cap has been flat/slightly declining at $301–$307B range, confirming capital rotation into crypto assets.

upcoming.title: PPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — pipeline inflation read one day before CPI (Sep 11) and six days before FOMC (Sep 16); July 2026 PPI was unchanged (final demand goods −0.7%, services +0.2%); markets pricing ~60% probability of a Sep 16 hike after August NFP beat (+162K vs +56K consensus, Sep 4); a hot PPI print would reinforce the hike case and could push DXY above 100 (headwind threshold for risk assets); a cooling PPI would add to the disinflationary narrative and reduce hike probability heading into CPI Sep 11; released same day as ECB rate decision (2:15 PM CET) and weekly jobless claims.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 6, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 6, 2026; prior week ending Aug 29 came in at 206,000; strong August NFP (+162K, Sep 4) confirmed labor market resilience; a spike in claims above 220K would temper the rate-hike narrative heading into CPI Sep 11 and FOMC Sep 16; released alongside PPI August and ECB rate decision — a triple-event day.

upcoming.title: ECB Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: European Central Bank Governing Council rate decision at 2:15 PM CET (8:15 AM ET), press conference at 2:45 PM CET; prior ECB hike was June 11, 2026 — the first in three years, citing Middle East conflict-driven energy price inflation; September move widely anticipated by markets; an ECB hike alongside a hot US PPI on Sep 10 would reinforce the global tightening narrative and could push DXY above 100 (headwind threshold for risk assets); ECB guidance on the pace of further tightening and updated staff projections will drive EUR/USD and global fixed income; also released same day: H.4.1 Fed balance sheet (week ending Sep 10) at 4:30 PM ET.

upcoming.title: CPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — final major inflation read before FOMC September 16; the data trifecta: NFP Sep 4 (+162K, hawkish), CPI Sep 11, then FOMC Sep 16; markets pricing ~60% probability of a hike after NFP beat; DXY at 98.97 — the CPI print is the key trigger for a directional break above 100 (headwind) or toward 97.5 (supportive); a hot CPI above 3.8% YoY would likely lock in a Sep 16 hike; a soft CPI below 3.3% would pull back hike expectations and support risk assets; July 2026 CPI was 3.6% YoY; core CPI ex-food and energy is the primary Fed focus.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Survey preliminary read for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — released same day as CPI August; captures 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations alongside current conditions and expectations indexes; elevated 1-year inflation expectations combined with hot CPI would strengthen the Fed's case for a Sep 16 hike; a drop in confidence alongside cooling CPI would temper hike odds and create a risk-asset supportive setup heading into FOMC; watch 5-year inflation expectations closely as a long-run anchoring signal for the Fed's reaction function.
